title: Total variation distance as half the $\ell^1$ distance
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set equipped with the discrete measurable structure, and let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on $\Omega$. Then the supremum form of total variation distance, $\mathrm{TV}_{\sup}(\mu,
u) = \sup\{|\mu(S) - 
u(S)| : S \subseteq \Omega\}$, is exactly half the $\ell^1$ distance between the two measures across the individual points:
\[
  \mathrm{TV}_{\sup}(\mu,
u) \;=\;  rac{1}{2}\sum_{\omega \in \Omega}  igl|\mu(\{\omega\}) - 
u(\{\omega\}) igr|.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $\Omega$ is a finite discrete measurable space
replaced:
On a finite measurable space $\Omega$, the supremum form of total variation distance
satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{TV}_{\sup}(\mu,\nu) \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\omega:\Omega}
    |\mu(\{\omega\}) - \nu(\{\omega\})|.
\]
